topic: Law of Contracts and Specific Relief: Specific Relief Act, 1963 (Remedies)
description: This module covers the Specific Relief Act, 1963, which provides equitable remedies for the enforcement of individual civil rights. It focuses on situations where monetary compensation (damages) is inadequate, detailing remedies like specific performance, injunctions, and declaratory decrees.

nature_and_specific_performance.concept: Nature of the Act and Specific Performance (Section 10)
key_points: Civil Rights Only: According to Section 4, specific relief can be granted only for the purpose of enforcing individual civil rights and not for the mere purpose of enforcing a penal law.
Specific Performance: This is an equitable remedy where the court orders a party to perform their exact obligations under a contract, rather than just paying damages for breach.

The 2018 Amendment Shift: Prior to 2018, granting specific performance was at the discretion of the court. The Specific Relief (Amendment) Act, 2018 fundamentally changed this by making specific performance a mandatory statutory right (subject to exceptions in Sections 11(2), 14, and 16), minimizing judicial discretion.
Substituted Performance: If a party has obtained substituted performance of the contract (got the job done by someone else under Section 20), they cannot seek specific performance.
Continuous Duty: Contracts the performance of which involves the performance of a continuous duty which the court cannot supervise.

Personal Qualifications: A contract which is so dependent on the personal qualifications or volition of the parties that the court cannot enforce specific performance of its material terms (e.g., a contract to paint a portrait, sing at a concert, or write a book).
Nature of Injunctions: Preventive relief is granted at the discretion of the court by injunction, temporary or perpetual. It is an order restraining a person from doing a particular act.
Temporary Injunctions (Section 37): These are granted for a specified time or until further orders of the court. They are regulated by the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), 1908.

Perpetual (Permanent) Injunctions (Section 38): Can only be granted by the decree made at the hearing and upon the merits of the suit. The defendant is permanently enjoined from the assertion of a right, or from the commission of an act, which would be contrary to the rights of the plaintiff.

questions.question: According to Section 4 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, specific relief can be granted for the enforcement of:

options.C: Both civil rights and penal laws

questions.explanation: Section 4 explicitly states that specific relief can be granted only for the purpose of enforcing individual civil rights and not for the mere purpose of enforcing a penal law.

questions.question: A famous artist signs a contract to paint a portrait of a businessman. A week later, the artist changes his mind and refuses to paint. The businessman sues for 'Specific Performance' to force the artist to complete the painting. Will the court grant this remedy?

options.A: Yes, because all valid contracts must be specifically performed after the 2018 amendment.
options.B: Yes, because the businessman has already paid the advance.
options.C: No, because under Section 14, a contract dependent on the personal qualifications or volition of a party (like artistic skill) cannot be specifically enforced.
options.D: No, because the Specific Relief Act only applies to real estate transactions.

questions.explanation: Under Section 14(c) of the Specific Relief Act, contracts that depend heavily on personal skills, qualifications, or volition (like painting, singing, or acting) are not specifically enforceable because a court cannot physically force someone to perform an artistic or highly personal act to a subjective standard.

questions.question: How did the Specific Relief (Amendment) Act, 2018 fundamentally alter the legal landscape regarding the 'Specific Performance' of contracts in India?

options.A: It completely abolished the remedy of specific performance, replacing it entirely with monetary damages.
options.B: It shifted specific performance from being a discretionary, exceptional remedy granted by courts to a general, mandatory statutory rule, subject to limited exceptions.
options.C: It restricted specific performance only to contracts involving the Union Government.
options.D: It made specific performance applicable to criminal offenses and penal laws.

questions.explanation: Prior to 2018, granting specific performance was largely at the court's discretion, and damages were the norm. The 2018 amendment changed the wording of Section 10 to mandate that specific performance 'shall be enforced', removing the court's general discretion and making it a primary statutory right (except in specific cases outlined in Sections 11, 14, and 16).
